title: Acid On, Acid Off
endLine: Food switches acid on; what flows downstream switches it off.

scenes.tts: The first film showed the gut wall keeping its own beat. The stomach runs one more machine: a pump. Its juice reaches about p H one. That is roughly a million times more acidic than inside the cell making it. What switches that pump on, and what switches it off?
scenes.narration: The first film showed the gut wall keeping its own beat. The stomach runs one more machine: a pump. Its juice reaches about pH 1. That is roughly a million times more acidic than inside the cell making it. What switches that pump on, and what switches it off?
scenes.caption: The first film showed the gut wall keeping its own beat. The stomach runs one more machine: a pump. Its juice reaches about pH 1. That is roughly a million times more acidic than inside the cell making it. What switches that pump on, and what switches it off?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's colour map: BLUE = smooth muscle wall; YELLOW = the slow-wave beat; GREEN = nerves and hormones that turn things on; ORANGE = gut contents; GREY = outlines. New in this film: MAGENTA = acid (hydrogen ions); CYAN = brake signals that turn acid down; WHITE = the mucus gel. ONE WORLD, kept all film: a large side-view cut of the stomach flowing into the duodenum, filling about 70% of the frame height. Upper left: the body of the stomach (label 'body'); lower right: the antrum (label 'antrum'); a narrow pylorus; then the duodenum running down the right edge (label 'duodenum'). The BLUE muscle wall carries faint YELLOW beat ticks that pulse slowly in place, a nod to the first film. On 'keeping its own beat', the YELLOW ticks brighten once and settle back. On 'a pump', a circular window opens on the lining of the body, magnifying one cell (label 'parietal cell'). On 'about pH 1', the lumen beside the cell fills with dense MAGENTA dots and a small vertical gauge beside the window drops to a mark labelled 'about pH 1'; inside the cell, only a few sparse MAGENTA dots drift. On 'a million times', a bracket joins the dense lumen and the sparse cell, labelled 'about a million-fold'. On the question, two empty switch icons appear above the window, labelled 'on?' and 'off?'.
Title 'Acid On, Acid Off' fades in across the top for 2 s while the 'on?' and 'off?' icons dim but stay. The stomach world keeps moving: YELLOW ticks pulse, MAGENTA dots drift in the lumen.

scenes.tts: At rest, the parietal cell keeps its pumps tucked inside small vesicles. When stimulated, it moves them into the membrane of a deep fold facing the lumen. Each cycle swaps a hydrogen ion out for a potassium ion, paid for with A T P. Chloride follows potassium out, so hydrochloric acid builds.
scenes.narration: At rest, the parietal cell keeps its pumps tucked inside small vesicles. When stimulated, it moves them into the membrane of a deep fold facing the lumen. Each cycle swaps a hydrogen ion out for a potassium ion, paid for with ATP. Chloride follows potassium out, so hydrochloric acid builds.
scenes.caption: At rest, the parietal cell keeps its pumps tucked inside small vesicles. When stimulated, it moves them into the membrane of a deep fold facing the lumen. Each cycle swaps a hydrogen ion out for a potassium ion, paid for with ATP. Chloride follows potassium out, so hydrochloric acid builds.
scenes.visual: The window on the parietal cell grows to fill about 65% of the frame height; the stomach world shrinks to a small inset at top right, still moving. Inside the cell: several small round vesicles, each carrying a plain turnstile icon (no molecular structure), labelled 'pumps, stored'. A deep fold runs from the lumen into the cell, labelled 'deep fold'. On 'when stimulated', the vesicles drift to the fold and merge into its membrane; the turnstiles now line the fold. On 'swaps', each turnstile turns: one MAGENTA dot goes out into the fold as one small GREY dot labelled 'potassium' comes in; a small token labelled 'ATP' flashes and fades at each turn. On 'Chloride follows', GREY potassium dots and pale GREY chloride dots leave together through side doors into the fold. MAGENTA dots accumulate in the fold; label 'hydrochloric acid'.

scenes.tts: Three signals turn the pump on: acetylcholine from nerves, histamine, and the hormone gastrin. The vagus nerve can start acid early. Sight, smell, taste and chewing switch it on before food arrives.
scenes.narration: Three signals turn the pump on: acetylcholine from nerves, histamine, and the hormone gastrin. The vagus nerve can start acid early. Sight, smell, taste and chewing switch it on before food arrives.
scenes.caption: Three signals turn the pump on: acetylcholine from nerves, histamine, and the hormone gastrin. The vagus nerve can start acid early. Sight, smell, taste and chewing switch it on before food arrives.
scenes.visual: Pull back: the parietal cell shrinks into its window on the body of the stomach; the full stomach-duodenum world returns. A small GREY neighbour cell sits beside the parietal cell, labelled 'ECL cell'. Three GREEN plugs arrive one at a time, each labelled: 'acetylcholine' docks on the parietal cell's blood-facing side; 'histamine' puffs from the ECL cell and docks there too; 'gastrin' docks mainly on the ECL cell, which puffs more histamine onto the parietal cell. Each step makes the turnstiles in the fold turn faster and MAGENTA dots pour out a little faster. On 'The vagus nerve', a GREEN wire descends from the top edge into the stomach wall, labelled 'vagus'. On 'Sight, smell, taste', four small icons (eye, nose, tongue, tooth) appear at top left and send pulses down the GREEN wire. The stomach lumen is still EMPTY of ORANGE food, yet MAGENTA acid already rises; tag 'before food' beside the empty lumen. The 'on?' icon above the window lights GREEN.

scenes.tts: Then food stretches the stomach, releasing more acetylcholine and gastrin. Digested protein also acts directly on G cells in the antrum. Gastrin travels in the blood to the body of the stomach, and acid climbs.
scenes.narration: Then food stretches the stomach, releasing more acetylcholine and gastrin. Digested protein also acts directly on G cells in the antrum. Gastrin travels in the blood to the body of the stomach, and acid climbs.
scenes.caption: Then food stretches the stomach, releasing more acetylcholine and gastrin. Digested protein also acts directly on G cells in the antrum. Gastrin travels in the blood to the body of the stomach, and acid climbs.
scenes.visual: ORANGE food blobs enter at the top of the stomach; the BLUE wall bows outward (label 'stretch'), and the GREEN vagus wire pulses brighter. In the antrum lining, a cell appears and is labelled 'G cell'. On 'Digested protein', small ORANGE fragments touch the G cell and it glows GREEN. On 'travels in the blood', GREEN gastrin dots leave the G cell into a thin GREY-outlined blood vessel (label 'blood') drawn along the outside of the wall, travel up to the body of the stomach, and dock mainly on the ECL cell, which puffs GREEN histamine onto the parietal cell. On 'acid climbs', MAGENTA dots in the lumen thicken and the small pH gauge drops further (schematic, no numbers).

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. Food arriving in a part of the gut turns that part on. What that part makes, or passes downstream, turns it back down. The stomach shows both halves.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. Food arriving in a part of the gut turns that part on. What that part makes, or passes downstream, turns it back down. The stomach shows both halves.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. Food arriving in a part of the gut turns that part on. What that part makes, or passes downstream, turns it back down. The stomach shows both halves.
scenes.visual: The world holds steady and keeps moving: ORANGE food and MAGENTA acid swirling slowly in the stomach. On 'Food arriving', a large GREEN arrow arcs from the incoming food to the parietal cell, labelled 'food turns on'. On 'turns it back down', a large CYAN arrow appears, starting at the MAGENTA acid in the lumen and pointing DOWNSTREAM toward the antrum and the duodenum, labelled 'downstream turns down'. Its far end is left open, with no target yet. On 'both halves', both arrows pulse once together.

scenes.tts: Acid made in the body of the stomach flows down to the antrum. There, acid makes D cells release somatostatin. Somatostatin holds back the G cells beside them. The more acid, the less gastrin.
scenes.narration: Acid made in the body of the stomach flows down to the antrum. There, acid makes D cells release somatostatin. Somatostatin holds back the G cells beside them. The more acid, the less gastrin.
scenes.caption: Acid made in the body of the stomach flows down to the antrum. There, acid makes D cells release somatostatin. Somatostatin holds back the G cells beside them. The more acid, the less gastrin.
scenes.visual: MAGENTA acid dots stream from the body of the stomach down into the antrum. Next to the GREEN G cell, a second cell appears, labelled 'D cell'. On 'release somatostatin', MAGENTA dots touch the D cell and it puffs CYAN dots, labelled 'somatostatin', onto the G cell. The G cell dims and its GREEN gastrin dots slow to a trickle. On 'The more acid', a two-step loop plays: more MAGENTA arrives, more CYAN puffs, fewer GREEN dots leave; then the cycle repeats once. Label under the antrum: 'more acid, less gastrin'. The CYAN arrow from s05 now reaches its first target, the antrum.

scenes.tts: Now the acidic, fatty chyme crosses into the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine. Will the duodenum call for more stomach acid, or less?
scenes.narration: Now the acidic, fatty chyme crosses into the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine. Will the duodenum call for more stomach acid, or less?
scenes.caption: Now the acidic, fatty chyme crosses into the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine. Will the duodenum call for more stomach acid, or less?
scenes.visual: A squirt of ORANGE chyme flecked with MAGENTA dots passes the pylorus into the duodenum. Small pale yellow droplets in the chyme are labelled 'fat'. The duodenum lining shows two still-unlabelled cells, dim. Question card at top in white: 'More acid, or less?' The parietal cell keeps pumping at its current rate.
Predict pause. The question card stays. The chyme drifts slowly down the duodenum; the two duodenal cells stay dim and unlabelled; YELLOW beat ticks keep pulsing in the wall. No other change.

scenes.tts: Less. Acid in the duodenum releases secretin from S cells. Fat and digested protein release C C K from I cells. Both inhibit gastric acid. C C K probably works through somatostatin.
scenes.narration: Less. Acid in the duodenum releases secretin from S cells. Fat and digested protein release CCK from I cells. Both inhibit gastric acid. CCK probably works through somatostatin.
scenes.caption: Less. Acid in the duodenum releases secretin from S cells. Fat and digested protein release CCK from I cells. Both inhibit gastric acid. CCK probably works through somatostatin.
scenes.visual: The question card dissolves. On 'secretin', MAGENTA dots touch the first duodenal cell, now labelled 'S cell', and it releases CYAN dots labelled 'secretin'. On 'CCK', fat droplets touch the second cell, labelled 'I cell', and it releases CYAN dots labelled 'CCK'. Both streams enter the blood vessel and travel back up to the body of the stomach. On 'inhibit gastric acid', the parietal cell's turnstiles slow and MAGENTA output thins. On 'probably', a small dashed CYAN path from CCK toward a somatostatin puff, tagged 'probably'.

scenes.tts: So the meal switches acid on in the stomach. It switches acid off from two places downstream of the pump: the antrum and the duodenum. Once chyme reaches the intestine, the signals are mostly a brake.
scenes.narration: So the meal switches acid on in the stomach. It switches acid off from two places downstream of the pump: the antrum and the duodenum. Once chyme reaches the intestine, the signals are mostly a brake.
scenes.caption: So the meal switches acid on in the stomach. It switches acid off from two places downstream of the pump: the antrum and the duodenum. Once chyme reaches the intestine, the signals are mostly a brake.
scenes.visual: The CYAN arrow from s05 now forks to reach both targets, the antrum and the duodenum, each with a CYAN brake pad icon labelled 'brake 1' (antrum) and 'brake 2' (duodenum). The GREEN arrow from food to the parietal cell stays bright. On 'mostly a brake', the duodenum's CYAN pad glows and the GREEN arrow dims slightly; MAGENTA output from the parietal cell thins (schematic, no numbers). The 'off?' icon above the window lights CYAN beside the GREEN 'on?' icon.

scenes.tts: The lining must survive the acid. Surface cells secrete bicarbonate, and a mucus gel traps it against the lining. So the surface stays far less acidic than the lumen. Tight junctions limit how much acid leaks back in.
scenes.narration: The lining must survive the acid. Surface cells secrete bicarbonate, and a mucus gel traps it against the lining. So the surface stays far less acidic than the lumen. Tight junctions limit how much acid leaks back in.
scenes.caption: The lining must survive the acid. Surface cells secrete bicarbonate, and a mucus gel traps it against the lining. So the surface stays far less acidic than the lumen. Tight junctions limit how much acid leaks back in.
scenes.visual: Zoom to a stretch of the lining in the body of the stomach, beside the parietal cell's window: a row of surface cells. A thick WHITE gel layer settles over them, labelled 'mucus gel'. Pale BLUE-WHITE dots, labelled 'bicarbonate', rise from the cells and stay trapped inside the gel. MAGENTA dots crowd the lumen side but thin out sharply inside the gel; a small two-point tag compares 'lumen: very acidic' with 'surface: far less'. On 'Tight junctions', short GREY seals between the surface cells glow; a single MAGENTA dot bounces off one seal.

scenes.tts: So acid is turned on by what arrives, and down by what the stomach sends onward. Acid brakes it from the antrum. Acid and fat brake it from the duodenum.
scenes.narration: So acid is turned on by what arrives, and down by what the stomach sends onward. Acid brakes it from the antrum. Acid and fat brake it from the duodenum.
scenes.caption: So acid is turned on by what arrives, and down by what the stomach sends onward. Acid brakes it from the antrum. Acid and fat brake it from the duodenum.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full stomach-duodenum world. On 'turned on by what arrives', the GREEN arrow from incoming ORANGE food to the parietal cell pulses; on 'what the stomach sends onward', ORANGE chyme with MAGENTA flecks moves through the pylorus and the forked CYAN arrow pulses. On 'from the antrum', the antrum's CYAN brake pad pulses as MAGENTA dots arrive; on 'from the duodenum', the duodenum's CYAN pad pulses as chyme with fat droplets arrives. The 'on?' and 'off?' icons have become a GREEN 'on' and a CYAN 'off'. MAGENTA output settles to a steady trickle (schematic).

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (YELLOW beat ticks pulsing, ORANGE chyme drifting into the duodenum, a slow MAGENTA trickle from the parietal cell). Large white text, centred: 'Food switches acid on; what flows downstream switches it off.'
